docs.title: gprop — 3D Urban RF Propagation Simulator
docs.text: gprop is a full end-to-end pipeline for predicting cellular network coverage in real urban environments. It takes real LiDAR point cloud data and OpenStreetMap building footprints, constructs a 3D digital twin of the area, and computes received signal strength across a grid — accounting for free-space path loss and multi-knife-edge diffraction through buildings and trees.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
# 1. Draw your scenario and save antenna positions
python3 bin/gui.py

# 2. Download LiDAR and building data
python3 bin/fetch.py

# 3. Build the digital twin
./bin/preproc lpc.laz buildings.wkt ground.tif

# 4. Compute coverage
OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 ./bin/prop topology.csv antenna.pat aoi.wkt buildings.csv trees.csv ground.tif

# 5. Generate heatmap
python3 bin/3DHeatMap.py --csv heatmap.csv --topology_csv topology.csv --outdir outputs

docs.text:
flowchart LR

docs.text: Section What you'll find Pipeline Step-by-step flow, inputs, and outputs for every stage Reference Exact file formats, CLI arguments, build system Algorithms How RANSAC, diffraction, and path loss work internally

docs.title: Key facts
docs.text:
• Languages: C99, C++17, Python 3
  • Libraries: PDAL, GDAL, GEOS, PROJ, Flask, Leaflet.js
  • Scale tested: 2,438 buildings · 12,491 tree clusters · 0.89 km² · 4 transmitters
  • Benchmarks: preproc ~218s · prop ~18s single-threaded, ~4s at 10 cores

docs.title: Knife-Edge Diffraction
docs.text: prop models signal attenuation through urban obstacles using the Fresnel-Kirchhoff knife-edge diffraction model applied sequentially across the dominant edges along each line-of-sight path.

docs.title: Profile construction
docs.text:
For each transmitter-receiver pair, populate_profile in diffraction.c:

  1. Uses Amanatides-Woo grid traversal to find all 10m tiles along the LOS
  2. For each tile, computes the minimum LOS elevation at the tile boundary
  3. Skips tiles where max_elev < min_los_elev (early exit)
  4. For surviving tiles, intersects the LOS segment against every building and tree footprint edge using 2D determinant intersection
  5. Each intersection point becomes an Edge with:
    • distance — 3D distance from transmitter to intersection point
    • elev — obstacle height above the LOS line (negative values discarded)

docs.title: Profile reduction
docs.text: process_profile retains only the convex hull of obstructions visible from the transmitter — edges dominated by a taller closer edge are pruned.

docs.title: Loss computation
docs.text:
For each retained edge the Fresnel-Kirchhoff diffraction parameter v is computed:

$$v = h \sqrt{\frac{2}{\lambda} \left(\frac{1}{d_1} + \frac{1}{d_2}\right)}$$

Where:

Symbol Meaning h Edge height above the LOS line between the two flanking points λ Wavelength (c / frequency) d₁ Distance from transmitter to the edge d₂ Distance from edge to receiver

The ITU-R approximation gives loss in dB:

$$L = 6.9 + 20 \log_{10}\left(\sqrt{(v - 0.1)^2 + 1} + v - 0.1\right) \quad \text{for } v > -0.78$$

$$L = 0 \text{ dB} \quad \text{for } v \leq -0.78 \text{ (clear LOS)}$$

docs.title: Multi-edge cascade
docs.text:
For multiple dominant edges, loss is accumulated hop by hop — a Deygout-style sequential cascade:

TX ──── edge₁ ──── edge₂ ──── ... ──── RX
        hop₁        hop₂
L_total = hop_loss(TX, edge₁, edge₂)
        + hop_loss(edge₁, edge₂, edge₃)
        + ...
        + hop_loss(edgeₙ₋₁, edgeₙ, RX)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Value Description PROFILE_EXT 100 Edge buffer growth step INITIAL_PROFILE_LEN 1000 Initial edge buffer allocation SCALE 10 m Tile size for grid traversal

docs.title: Path Loss Models
docs.text: prop supports three base path loss models, selectable at compile time. All models are combined with antenna gain from the radiation pattern.

docs.title: Free-Space Path Loss (FSPL)
docs.text:
The theoretical baseline assuming no environmental clutter — only distance and frequency.

$$L_{FSPL} = 20 \log_{10}\left(\frac{4\pi d f}{c}\right)$$

Symbol Meaning d 3D distance from transmitter to receiver (metres) f Carrier frequency (Hz) c Speed of light (3×10⁸ m/s)

docs.title: Log-Distance
docs.text:
Extends FSPL with an empirical path loss exponent n to account for the environment.

$$L = L_{FSPL}(1\text{m}) + 10n \log_{10}(d)$$

n value Environment 2.0 Free space 2.5–3.0 Suburban 3.0–4.0 Urban 4.0–5.0 Dense urban / indoor

docs.title: Alpha-Beta
docs.text:
A frequency-aware empirical model used in 5G planning.

$$L = 10\alpha \log_{10}(d) + \beta + 10 \log_{10}\left(\frac{f}{1 \text{ GHz}}\right)$$

docs.title: Antenna gain
docs.text:
The effective antenna gain for any receiver position combines the boresight gain with horizontal and vertical pattern attenuation:

$$G_{effective} = G_{max} + H[\theta] + V[\phi]$$

Symbol Meaning G_max Boresight gain from topology.csv (dBi) H[θ] Horizontal pattern attenuation at relative azimuth θ (dB, ≤ 0) V[φ] Vertical pattern attenuation at relative downtilt φ (dB, ≤ 0) θ atan2(Δx, Δy) − antenna azimuth, rounded to nearest degree φ −atan2(Δz, horizontal_distance) + antenna downtilt, rounded to nearest degree

docs.title: Final RSS
docs.text:
$$RSS = P_{tx} - L_{base} - L_{diffraction}$$

All in dBm / dB. The best RSS across all transmitters is written to heatmap.csv.

docs.title: RANSAC Plane Segmentation
docs.text: preproc uses RANSAC (Random Sample Consensus) with region growing and PCA refinement to extract building roof planes from LiDAR point clouds.

docs.title: Why RANSAC
docs.text: Building LiDAR scans contain many outliers — vegetation touching rooftops, scan overlap noise, and edge artefacts. Least-squares plane fitting is highly sensitive to outliers. RANSAC finds the best plane fit by design, ignoring outliers through random sampling.

docs.title: Algorithm steps
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Pick random seed point] --> B[Find 50 nearest neighbours via KD-tree]
    B --> C[Sample 3-point subset randomly]
    C --> D[Fit plane via cross product]
    D --> E{40+ inliers within 0.1m AND normal.z >= 0.5?}
    E -->|no, retry up to MAX_SEED_TRIALS| C
    E -->|yes| F[Add inliers to cluster]
    F --> G[Region growing: expand in steps of 20 KNN]
    G --> H{10 consecutive empty extensions?}
    H -->|no| G
    H -->|yes| I[PCA refinement: build 3x3 covariance matrix]
    I --> J[Find minimum eigenvalue analytically]
    J --> K[Update plane normal from eigenvector]
    K --> L{Coincident with existing plane?}
    L -->|yes| M[Merge clusters]
    L -->|no| N[Add as new plane]
    N --> O[Outlier pruning: remove points with fewer than 6 of 10 neighbours in cluster]
    O --> P[Compute concave hull footprint]
    P --> Q[Intersect with OSM building polygon]
    Q --> R[Write to buildings.csv]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Value Effect INITIAL_KNN 50 Neighbourhood for seed search MIN_INITIAL_POINTS 40 Minimum inliers to accept seed plane THRESH 0.1 m Inlier distance threshold MAX_SEED_RETRIES 5000 Max seed points to try before giving up MAX_SEED_TRIALS 100 Max 3-point samples per seed MIN_NORMAL_Z 0.5 Minimum vertical component — filters walls EXTENSION_KNN 20 Region growing step size MAX_FAILS 10 Consecutive empty extensions before stopping NORMAL_DEVIATION 0.2 Max normal difference for plane merging OFFSET_DEVIATION 0.1 m Max offset difference for plane merging PRUNE_KNN 10 Neighbours checked during outlier pruning PRUNE_CONSENSUS 6 Minimum in-cluster neighbours to keep a point MAX_PLANES 10 Maximum roof facets per building

docs.title: Euclidean tree clustering
docs.text:
Points not belonging to any building are clustered into individual trees using 2D Euclidean clustering (XY only).

Parameter Value Effect MAX_DISTANCE 0.6 m Maximum distance to join a cluster MAX_CLUSTER_POINTS 500 KNN search radius MIN_CLUSTER_POINTS 50 Minimum points to accept cluster MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILS 500 Points checked without join before stopping

docs.title: Stage 2 — Data Acquisition (fetch.py)
docs.text: fetch.py downloads all geospatial data needed to build the digital twin. It queries two data sources — USGS 3DEP LiDAR from AWS S3, and OpenStreetMap building footprints via the Overpass API.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
python3 bin/fetch.py

When prompted, paste the WKT polygon from aoi.wkt:

Enter WKT polygon covering area of interest: POLYGON((-78.875 42.895, ...))

Tip

The contents of aoi.wkt is exactly what to paste here. Run cat aoi.wkt to see it.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Source Description WKT polygon (stdin) Pasted from aoi.wkt Area of interest in EPSG:4326 USGS 3DEP Entwine AWS S3 LiDAR point tiles covering the AoI OSM Overpass API Internet Building footprint polygons

docs.title: Processing steps
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Read AoI polygon from stdin] --> B[Query OSM Overpass API]
    A --> C[Find intersecting USGS LiDAR projects]
    B --> D[Write buildings.wkt]
    C --> E[Download LAZ tiles from AWS S3 via PDAL EPT reader]
    E --> F[Clip to AoI]
    E --> G[Filter to ground points only Classification == 2]
    G --> H[Generate 1m DSM with GDAL writers.gdal]
    H --> I[Patch holes with gdal_fillnodata]
    F --> J[Remove ground + outlier points from LAZ]
    J --> K[Write lpc.laz]

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: File Format CRS Description lpc.laz LAZ (compressed LAS) EPSG:3857 Non-ground, non-outlier LiDAR points buildings.wkt Plain text EPSG:3857 One WKT polygon per line ground.tif GeoTIFF, 1 band Float64 EPSG:3857 1m bare-earth digital surface model

docs.title: ground.tif properties
docs.text:
• Resolution: 1m × 1m
  • Band: 1 (elevation in metres above sea level)
  • NoData holes filled by gdal_fillnodata

docs.title: Point cloud filters applied to lpc.laz
docs.text:
Filter PDAL expression Removes Ground points Classification != 2 Bare earth returns Outliers Classification != 7 && Classification != 18 Low/high noise Low vegetation HeightAboveGround >= 2 Grass, shrubs under 2m

Common error

If you see readers.ept: Could not read from 's3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/...', the S3 endpoint is stale. In fetch.py replace s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com with s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com.

docs.title: Stage 1 — GUI (gui.py)
docs.text: gui.py is the entry point of the pipeline. It starts a local Flask web server and opens a browser-based map editor where you draw the area of interest and place antenna base stations.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
python3 bin/gui.py

A browser opens at http://127.0.0.1:5000. When finished, press ENTER in the terminal.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: None — this is the first stage. All data is entered interactively in the browser.

docs.title: What you do in the browser
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Open geojson_creator.html] --> B[Draw AoI polygon]
    B --> C[Place antenna markers]
    C --> D[Fill in antenna properties]
    D --> E[Click Save]
    E --> F[Press ENTER in terminal]

Antenna properties per marker:

Field Unit Description azimuth degrees Horizontal pointing direction, 0 = North frequency MHz Carrier frequency Ptx (power) dBm Transmit power Gtx (gain) dBi Antenna boresight gain height m Height above ground

docs.text: File Format Description scenario.geojson GeoJSON Raw drawn features — polygon + point markers aoi.wkt Plain text First feature (polygon) as WKT in EPSG:4326, one line topology.csv CSV One antenna per line, 8 columns, no header

docs.text:
lon,lat,height_m,azimuth_deg,downtilt_deg,freq_MHz,power_dBm,gain_dBi
-78.8645,42.9067,20.0,90.0,-1.0,3560.0,43.0,17.0
-78.8650,42.9070,18.0,180.0,-1.0,3640.0,43.0,17.0

Downtilt

Downtilt is hardcoded to -1.0 in the GUI. Edit topology.csv directly after saving if you need a specific mechanical downtilt value.

docs.title: Stage 5 — Heatmap Generation (3DHeatMap.py)
docs.text: 3DHeatMap.py reads the raw RSS grid from heatmap.csv, applies Gaussian smoothing, renders it on an OpenStreetMap basemap, and packages everything as a KMZ file for Google Earth.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
python3 bin/3DHeatMap.py \
  --csv heatmap.csv \
  --topology_csv topology.csv \
  --outdir outputs \
  --out_prefix my_coverage

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: File Format Description heatmap.csv CSV X, Y (EPSG:3857), RSS (dBm) from prop topology.csv CSV Antenna positions and azimuths for arrow overlay

docs.title: Processing steps
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Read heatmap.csv] --> B[Clean invalid rows]
    B --> C[Aggregate XY points into grid cells]
    C --> D[Gaussian smoothing sigma]
    D --> E[Mask cells below min_weight threshold]
    E --> F[Render on OSM basemap with contextily]
    F --> G[Export PNG with colorbar]
    G --> H[Export transparent PNG overlay]
    H --> I[Export GeoTIFF in EPSG:3857]
    I --> J[Compute antenna arrow geometry from azimuth]
    J --> K[Write KML with GroundOverlay and ScreenOverlay]
    K --> L[Package into KMZ]

docs.text:
The heatmap uses a fixed RSRP scale:

Colour RSS range Meaning Red / yellow -60 to -75 dBm Strong signal Green -75 to -95 dBm Usable signal Blue / purple -95 to -120 dBm Weak signal Transparent below -120 dBm No coverage

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text: gprop is organised as five sequential stages. Each stage produces files consumed by the next. Stages 3 and 4 (preproc and prop) are pre-compiled C binaries; the rest are Python scripts.

docs.title: Full data flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph stage1["Stage 1 — gui.py"]
        G1[Draw AoI polygon]
        G2[Place antenna markers]
        G3[Set azimuth / freq / power / gain / height]
        G1 --> G2 --> G3
    end

    subgraph stage2["Stage 2 — fetch.py"]
        F1[Query USGS 3DEP LiDAR]
        F2[Query OSM Overpass API]
        F3[Generate bare-earth DSM]
        F1 --> F3
        F2 --> F3
    end

    subgraph stage3["Stage 3 — preproc (C binary)"]
        P1[Read LAZ point cloud]
        P2[Assign points to building footprints]
        P3[RANSAC plane segmentation]
        P4[Euclidean tree clustering]
        P1 --> P2 --> P3
        P1 --> P2 --> P4
    end

    subgraph stage4["Stage 4 — prop (C binary)"]
        R1[Load digital twin into tile grid]
        R2[For each 5m grid point inside AoI]
        R3[Compute diffraction loss along LOS]
        R4[Compute FSPL and antenna gain]
        R5[Write best RSS across all Tx]
        R1 --> R2 --> R3 --> R4 --> R5
    end

    subgraph stage5["Stage 5 — 3DHeatMap.py"]
        H1[Read heatmap.csv]
        H2[Gaussian smoothing]
        H3[Render on OSM basemap]
        H4[Export KML/KMZ]
        H1 --> H2 --> H3 --> H4
    end

    stage1 -->|"aoi.wkt, topology.csv"| stage2
    stage2 -->|"lpc.laz, buildings.wkt, ground.tif"| stage3
    stage3 -->|"buildings.csv, trees.csv"| stage4
    stage4 -->|"heatmap.csv"| stage5

docs.title: Stage 3 — Preprocessing (preproc)
docs.text: preproc is a compiled C binary that constructs the 3D digital twin from raw LiDAR and building footprint data. It segments the point cloud into building roof planes and vegetation clusters.

docs.title: Run
docs.text: ./bin/preproc lpc.laz buildings.wkt ground.tif

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Argument File Format Description argv[1] lpc.laz LAZ Non-ground LiDAR point cloud argv[2] buildings.wkt Plain text OSM building footprints, one WKT per line, EPSG:3857 argv[3] ground.tif GeoTIFF 1m bare-earth DSM

docs.title: Processing steps
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Read LAZ via PDAL] --> B[Read building footprints via GEOS WKT reader]
    B --> C[Read DSM via GDAL]
    C --> D[assign_indices: sort points into building footprints]
    D --> E{Point inside a building?}
    E -->|yes| F[Add to building point set]
    E -->|no| G[Add to remaining outdoor set]
    F --> H[cluster_planes: RANSAC per building]
    H --> I[PCA plane refinement]
    I --> J[Coincident plane merging]
    J --> K[Outlier pruning]
    G --> L[cluster_trees: Euclidean clustering]
    K --> M[Write buildings.csv and buildings.ply]
    L --> N[Write trees.csv and trees.ply]
    K --> O[Write out.laz]

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: File Format Description buildings.csv CSV One roof plane per line: WKT footprint, a, b, c, d coefficients trees.csv CSV One tree cluster per line: WKT footprint, max elevation buildings.ply PLY ASCII 3D mesh of all building roof planes trees.ply PLY ASCII 3D double-cone mesh of all tree clusters out.laz LAZ Segmented point cloud with per-plane classification IDs

docs.title: buildings.csv format
docs.text:
"POLYGON ((x1 y1, x2 y2, ...))",a,b,c,d

The plane equation is ax + by + cz = d, giving roof elevation at any (x,y) as z = (d - ax - by) / c.

docs.title: trees.csv format
docs.text: "POLYGON ((x1 y1, x2 y2, ...))",max_elevation_metres

docs.title: Segmentation parameters
docs.text: Parameter Value Effect INITIAL_KNN 50 Neighbours searched for RANSAC seed MIN_INITIAL_POINTS 40 Minimum inliers required to accept a plane THRESH 0.1 m Maximum distance from plane to count as inlier MIN_NORMAL_Z 0.5 Filters out near-vertical planes (walls) MAX_PLANES 10 Maximum roof facets per building MAX_DISTANCE 0.6 m Euclidean cluster radius for trees MIN_CLUSTER_POINTS 50 Minimum points to accept a tree cluster

Runtime

preproc takes ~218s on real data (2,438 buildings). Run it once per area — reuse buildings.csv and trees.csv for all subsequent prop runs.

docs.title: Stage 4 — Propagation (prop)
docs.text: prop is a compiled C binary that computes received signal strength (RSS) at every 5m grid point inside the area of interest. It loads the digital twin produced by preproc and models signal propagation using free-space path loss and multi-knife-edge diffraction.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
# single-threaded
./bin/prop topology.csv antenna.pat aoi.wkt buildings.csv trees.csv ground.tif

# multi-threaded (recommended)
OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 ./bin/prop topology.csv antenna.pat aoi.wkt buildings.csv trees.csv ground.tif

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Argument File Format Description argv[1] topology.csv CSV Antenna parameters, 8 columns, no header argv[2] antenna.pat Plain text 541 dB attenuation values, one per line argv[3] aoi.wkt Plain text Area of interest polygon in EPSG:4326 argv[4] buildings.csv CSV Roof plane equations from preproc argv[5] trees.csv CSV Tree cluster data from preproc argv[6] ground.tif GeoTIFF 1m bare-earth DSM

docs.title: topology.csv column order
docs.text:
lon, lat, height_above_ground_m, azimuth_deg, downtilt_deg, freq_MHz, power_dBm, gain_dBi

-78.8645,42.9067,20.0,90.0,-1.0,3560.0,43.0,17.0

docs.title: antenna.pat format
docs.text:
541 lines total. No header. One dB attenuation value per line.

Lines 1–360    → horizontal pattern, degrees 0–359
                 0.0 dB at boresight, negative values = attenuation
Lines 361–541  → vertical pattern, degrees 0–180
                 line 361+90 = 451 is horizontal boresight (0.0 dB)

docs.title: Processing steps
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Read topology.csv] --> B[Project lat/lon to EPSG:3857 via PROJ]
    B --> C[Read antenna.pat]
    C --> D[init_twin: load buildings.csv and trees.csv]
    D --> E[Build 10m tile grid with Amanatides-Woo traversal]
    E --> F[Read ground.tif DSM]
    F --> G[For every 5m grid point inside AoI polygon]
    G --> H[ground_elevation lookup from DSM]
    H --> I[Set RX height = ground + 2m]
    I --> J[diffraction_loss: build LOS profile]
    J --> K[Intersect LOS with building and tree footprint edges]
    K --> L[Prune dominated edges]
    L --> M[Fresnel-Kirchhoff knife-edge loss per hop]
    M --> N[base_loss: FSPL + antenna gain from pattern]
    N --> O[RSS = power - diffraction_loss - base_loss]
    O --> P[Keep max RSS across all Tx]
    P --> Q[Write to heatmap.csv]
    G --> G

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: File Format Description heatmap.csv CSV X (EPSG:3857), Y (EPSG:3857), RSS (dBm) per grid point

docs.title: Key parameters (hardcoded in prop.c)
docs.text: Parameter Value Description HEATMAP_RESOLUTION 5 m Grid spacing RX_HAG 2 m Receiver height above ground SCALE 10 m Tile size for spatial indexing INITIAL_PROFILE_LEN 1000 Initial edge buffer for diffraction

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Cores Mean runtime 1 22,317 ms 2 11,548 ms 4 6,112 ms 8 4,542 ms 10 4,061 ms

Set OMP_NUM_THREADS to control thread count. Optimal is 4–8 for this workload — scaling becomes sub-linear above 8 due to memory bandwidth.

docs.title: Build System
docs.text: gprop uses a two-level POSIX Makefile system. The root Makefile dispatches to sub-Makefiles in preproc/ and prop/ with platform-specific variables.

docs.title: Build commands
docs.text:
macOSLinuxWindows 
make TARGET=darwin

make TARGET=linux

make TARGET=windows

Binaries are written to bin/preproc and bin/prop.

macOS (Homebrew)Linux (apt)Windows (Conda) 
brew install pdal gdal geos proj gcc make

apt install libpdal-dev libgdal-dev libgeos-dev libproj-dev gcc g++ make

conda install -c conda-forge pdal gdal geos proj -y

docs.title: prop
docs.text:
./bin/prop <topology> <pattern> <aoi> <buildings> <trees> <ground>

# with multithreading
OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 ./bin/prop ...
Position Argument Description 1 topology Path to topology.csv 2 pattern Path to antenna.pat (541 lines) 3 aoi Path to aoi.wkt (EPSG:4326 polygon) 4 buildings Path to buildings.csv from preproc 5 trees Path to trees.csv from preproc 6 ground Path to ground.tif DSM

Output heatmap.csv is written to the current working directory.

Environment variables:

Variable Default Description OMP_NUM_THREADS system cores Number of OpenMP threads

Argument Default Description --csv heatmap1.csv RSS grid CSV --x X X column name --y Y Y column name --rsrp RSS Signal column name --topology_csv topology.csv Antenna topology --cell 1.0 Grid cell size (m) --sigma 5.0 Gaussian blur (grid cells) --min_weight 0.02 Mask threshold --alpha 0.60 Heatmap transparency --cmap turbo Matplotlib colourmap --antenna_length_m 120 Arrow length (m) --arrow_head_m 25 Arrowhead size (m) --arrow_head_angle_deg 25 Arrowhead angle --antenna_line_width 5 Arrow line thickness --antenna_label_scale 2.0 Label scale in Google Earth --outdir outputs Output directory --out_prefix rsrp0_dummy Filename prefix

docs.title: File Formats
docs.text: Complete specification of every file in the gprop pipeline.

docs.title: aoi.wkt
docs.text:
Plain text, single line, WKT polygon in EPSG:4326 (longitude/latitude).

POLYGON ((-78.875 42.895, -78.855 42.895, -78.855 42.915, -78.875 42.915, -78.875 42.895))
  • First coordinate = last coordinate (closed ring)
  • Longitude first, latitude second
  • Written by gui.py, read by fetch.py and prop

docs.title: topology.csv
docs.text:
CSV, no header, 8 columns per line.

lon,lat,height_m,azimuth_deg,downtilt_deg,freq_MHz,power_dBm,gain_dBi
-78.8645,42.9067,20.0,90.0,-1.0,3560.0,43.0,17.0
Column Type Unit Description lon float degrees Antenna longitude lat float degrees Antenna latitude height float m Height above ground level azimuth float degrees Horizontal pointing, 0 = North downtilt float degrees Mechanical downtilt, negative = downward freq float MHz Carrier frequency power float dBm Transmit power gain float dBi Boresight antenna gain

docs.title: antenna.pat
docs.text:
Plain text, 541 lines, one dB attenuation value per line. No header.

Lines 1–360    horizontal pattern (degrees 0–359)
Lines 361–541  vertical pattern (degrees 0–180)
  • Values are attenuation relative to boresight (negative or zero)
  • 0.0 dB = boresight direction, maximum gain
  • -25.0 dB = 25 dB below boresight

docs.title: buildings.wkt
docs.text:
Plain text, one WKT polygon per line, EPSG:3857.

POLYGON ((748232.1 6421847.3, 748250.4 6421847.3, ...))
  • Written by fetch.py from OSM data
  • Easting/northing in metres (web Mercator)

docs.title: buildings.csv
docs.text:
CSV written by preproc. One roof plane facet per line.

"POLYGON ((x1 y1, x2 y2, ...))",a,b,c,d
Field Description WKT (quoted) 2D footprint of the roof plane in EPSG:3857 a, b, c Normal vector components of the roof plane d Plane offset — elevation at point (x,y) = (d − ax − by) / c

docs.title: trees.csv
docs.text:
CSV written by preproc. One tree cluster per line.

"POLYGON ((x1 y1, x2 y2, ...))",max_elevation
Field Description WKT (quoted) 2D footprint of the tree cluster crown in EPSG:3857 max_elevation Highest point in the cluster, metres above sea level

docs.title: ground.tif
docs.text:
GeoTIFF, single Float64 band, EPSG:3857, 1m resolution.

  • Values: elevation in metres above sea level
  • Holes (NoData) filled by gdal_fillnodata
  • Written by fetch.py, read by preproc and prop

docs.title: heatmap.csv
docs.text:
CSV written by prop. Three columns, no header.

x_epsg3857,y_epsg3857,rss_dbm
-8771523.6917,5309832.0847,-86.52
Column Unit Description X metres Easting in EPSG:3857 Y metres Northing in EPSG:3857 RSS dBm Best received signal strength across all transmitters
  • Grid spacing: 5m
  • Only points inside aoi.wkt are included
  • RSS = transmit power − free-space path loss − diffraction loss + antenna gain
